This document outlines the equipment inspection I1 to be performed on an 
 annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block

The governor power supply furnishes various regulated DC voltages to the 
 electronic portion of the governor by means of a DC/DC converter which is 
 supplied by two separate power sources : AC station service (220 Vac) through 
 an isolation transformer, it is then rectified and filtered, the resultant DC 
 is then paralleled with DC output of pre-regulator (the six zener diode), 
 which is supplied by DC station battery (220 Vdc)
The DC outputs of converter + 15 V, +12V, +5V, -15V

Each of the four regulated outputs has over voltage protector which is located 
 in the crowbar circuit
Each output also has under voltage protector which is located in monitor board

This document initiated by eng. Mahmoud Sayed Mahmoud, tested by eng. Hassan 
 Ahmad Abou El-Haggag, accepted by eng. Selim Ahmad Aly Selim, accepted by eng. 
 Abd el-Naby Abd El-Ghany High Dam Hydraulic Power 
 Station head sector and certified by eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman: HPGC quality 
 general director & MPIS coordinator

items:
A work permit must be issued, the 
 maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety ID category

Safety fence with caution marks 
 surrounding the work area is required

Wear the safety and healthy 
 protective equipment as safety shoes, helmet .... etc

Turn switches F403 (220 Vdc) & 
 F506 (220 Vac) "on"

Turn the transfer switch to "off" 
 / "test" position, as request
Unit out of service
Set of common and screw drivers
Digital multimeter

Turn the transfer switch to "off" position and then pull all modules out of 
 racks
Turn the transfer switch to "test" position

Check the old indication marker "AC supply" and "DC supply" to be sure they 
 are light indication both power sources are active, (figure 1)

Measure the voltage between the brown test points marked "125 Vdc" and "0 
 Vdc" 
 this voltage should be between 90 Vdc to 125 Vdc (the acceptable input range 
 for DC/DC converter) but the best value is 110 Vdc

Turn the potentiometers (P1,P2,P3,P4) which are located in the power supply 
 monitor board, fully counter - clockwise (figure 1)
 Note : the power supply voltage adjustments and the crowbar adjustments are 
 located inside the DC/DC converter

Adjust the + 15 Vdc supply to + 14.5 Vdc adjust P1 clockwise until the "+15 V 
 supply" indicating light goes out

Adjust the + 12 Vdc supply to + 11.5 Vdc adjust P2 clockwise until the "+12 V 
 supply" indicating light goes out

Adjust the + 5 Vdc supply to + 4.75 Vdc adjust P3 clockwise until the "+5 V 
 supply" indicating light goes out

Adjust the - 15 Vdc supply to - 14.5 Vdc adjust P4 clockwise until the "-15 V 
 supply" indicating light goes out

In order to calibrate the crowbar circuit adjust each of the voltage 
 regulators to the desired crowbar set voltage (+15V, +12V, +5V, -15V)

Slowly turn the crowbar adjustment counter clockwise for + 15 Vdc supply until 
 the voltage drop suddenly record this value in test sheet
Repeat step #9 for + 12 Vdc supply, + 5 Vdc supply and -15 Vdc supply

Shut off the power (turn the transfer switch to "off" position) and turn back 
 the voltage adjustments somewhat so the crowbar will not clamp the voltage 
 when power supply is reapplied (turn the transfer switch to "test" position) 
 the voltage regulators then may be calibrated for the specified output 
 voltages

Check and adjust each of the voltage regulators to the specified output 
 voltages (+15 V, +12V, +5V, -15V)

Plug in all modules, one at a time and make sure that the power supply 
 voltages remain constant

After all the modules are plugged in turn the transfer switch to "Gov" 
 position
